title: Know your enemy
say: The Ministry has surveyed all three fronts at every difficulty. It regrets to report that the Illuminate always know where you are.
changes: Difficulty and squad size now change ratings on every front: anti-tank and crowd clear count for more at high difficulty or with fewer players, and anti-tank for less at low difficulty.
Automatons and Illuminate count as slightly harder than Terminids. About now explains peril.
Against the Illuminate, stealth helps less because Stingrays find you anywhere, the Spear and W.A.S.P. help against Stingrays, and anti-tank helps from difficulty 8, where Leviathans spawn.
True Grit works on a ladder: most for a long stationary reload like the Recoilless Rifle, less for a long one, a little for the Stalwart.
New rules for rain, burning planets, Automaton explosives from difficulty 6, Blitz and Commando, and storms now cost long range weapons less.
Builds now note fire without fire resistance, no close range weapon in a storm, and overlapping support weapons. Close blasts like the Autocannon's are marked on the row.

title: Straight from the source
say: Weapon figures now come from the game itself. The Ministry thanks the wiki for its years of loyal service, which continue for everything else.
changes: Damage, armour penetration, magazines, rate of fire and handling for 105 weapons come from the game files.
Each weapon shows its loudness: Suppressed, Small, Medium, Large or Huge.
With 1 or 2 players, louder weapons draw more patrols on every front: quiet SMGs lose less, the Autocannon and launchers more. Terminids and Illuminate count it at six tenths.
The Rocket Sentry now has damage figures, and the Belt-Fed Grenade Launcher fires at 240 rpm.
About lists the game files as the source, and the wiki for what they do not cover.
A new tab icon: the Helldiver skull, half of it rebuilt in steel with a red optic.

title: Plain speech
say: The Ministry has reviewed every sentence in the tool and found most of them too long. Fewer words, same truth.
changes: Every rule has a short name that says what it does and when, with its full reason on hover.
Hovering a label, a rating or a reason opens a tooltip in the tool's own style.
An opened tier row is shorter: armour reads as full damage, reduced damage and weak points by name, and missing figures are marked.
Item notes keep only the one fact the row does not already show.
Every screen says less and says it plainly: warnings, suggestions, Collection, the Armoury, the war room and the Rules page.
About has a new How the rating works section: the maths, the sources and the list of missing data.

title: Reload discipline
say: The Ministry has reviewed how long you spend reloading and finds it excessive. Corrective armour is available.
changes: The picker says what a pick fixes: open the support slot on an Eruptor build and the Stalwart reads "Closes: No crowd clear in your hands".
True Grit does a little for big belts with a long reload, so the Stalwart and the Machine Gun now gain from it.
Siege-Ready reaches the Explosive Crossbow, and explosive resistance counts the Plasma Punisher as a blast you set off close.
An expendable launcher beside another support weapon warns you that one gets dropped for the other. No points lost: bringing launchers for the squad is allowed.
Reloading the page while editing a saved build opens that build again, not an empty one.

title: Know the ground you die on
say: Every armour set is now on file, and so is the planet. Excuses about the terrain will no longer be accepted.
changes: Every armour set in the game, 110 of them with their art: pick one under its passive in the builder, and its weight, armour, speed and stamina come with it.
Armour weight counts: heavy armour wants Stamina Enhancement and a Jump or Warp Pack, light armour the Shield Generator Pack, and heavy is better against bots than bugs.
The ground matters: Muscle Enhancement on swamps and snow, Jump Packs on cliffs, Warp Packs through city walls and two person bunker doors, and FRVs that like dunes and hate rocks.
The mission's clock matters: three Orbital Lasers fit a fifteen minute Eradicate.
More pairings: explosive resistance beside your own blasts, Siege-Ready beside an Eruptor or a shotgun, Med-Kit beside the Stim Pistol, and the Ballistic Shield wants a one handed primary.
Armour sets from a warbond you do not own are hidden with the rest of your locked gear.

title: Your armour has opinions now
say: Equipment works better together. The Ministry regrets that this took a memo.
changes: Armour passives now pair with the rest of your build: True Grit with a long or rooted reload, Gunslinger with a real pistol, melee armour with a blade, and fire, arc or gas resistance with gear of the same kind.
The builder's picker sees the build you are making, so a Cremator lifts fire resistant armour and True Grit lifts a Recoilless as you choose.
The Cremator earns its keep in Eradicate and defence missions, where you hold one spot and they keep coming.
Stealth is for one or two of you now, from solo on Suicide Mission or two of you on Impossible. A full squad on Super Helldive is trusted to know what it is doing.
Silenced weapons and stealth armour count against bugs and squids too, a little less than against bots, and a silenced gun without stealth armour counts for less.
Support weapons and sidearms carry their reload times, read from the wiki.
The Rules page has a new group, What it is paired with, for the twenty rules that read a whole build.

title: Declare your equipment, citizen
say: The Ministry cannot recommend what you do not own. It has tried.
changes: Until your collection is filled in, Drop Bay, the Armoury and the Tier Lists say so, with one click to set it up or to declare that you own everything.
Collection opens with a quick start, new player or veteran, and a short guide to what each of its buttons does.
The tour now starts in Collection and stops at every kind of button there.

title: Orientation is now mandatory
say: Attendance is voluntary. Non-attendance has been noted.
changes: A Democracy Officer gives new recruits a guided tour of the tool, one lit-up stop at a time. Settings has the refresher.
The Roadmap runs left to right, Shipped to Later, with one card per milestone that folds open.
The Changelog hangs off a timeline by month, and can be unfolded whole for the thorough citizen.

title: The tier list reports back for duty
say: Fewer clicks between you and your loadout. Efficiency is patriotism.
changes: The tier list is back in the menu, with the front, difficulty and how many of you on the page itself. Flip a rule off and watch the list move.
Drop Bay has a proper DROP button. Your slot no longer asks you to merely confirm your commitment to Democracy.
The war room's difficulty floats in a card under the map, with how many of you beside it and what each level brings as tiles instead of a paragraph.
Adjust scenario glows in your theme's colour, so the way into the war room is hard to miss.
The full name under the wordmark sits in two tidy lines on every theme. The Aquila was asked to breathe in slightly.
The last traces of the old name are gone, apart from the folder it lives in.

title: D.I.L.A.S., the war room and the Star Map
say: New name, new address, same unwavering commitment to Managed Democracy.
changes: D.D.S. is now D.I.L.A.S., the Democratic Intelligent Loadout & Armoury System, at dilas.me. Export your collection at the old address and Import it here, once.
Drop Bay is the front door. It suggests three of your own builds for this drop, says why each fits, and lets you adjust one without leaving.
Squad up with a six character code. Everybody's confirmed loadout lands in their slot, and the host's scenario becomes everybody's. No account needed.
The war room: the galaxy map across the whole screen, coloured with the live war, the Major Order and its medals over the top, and a planner that says where to go.
The Star Map, for reading the war: every front, each planet's intel, its history hour by hour, and one click to drop there.
The Armoury keeps your builds, shows what you have for each occasion on each front, and remembers every drop you confirmed.
The Rules page lists every rule behind our rating, what it moves where you are going, and a switch to turn it off.
Commando missions are Automaton only and play like it: no reinforcement boosters, and weapons that need no ammo rise.
Share a build as a link. Whoever opens it can keep a copy, or keep it and drop with it.

title: Drop Bay becomes the drop screen
say: The thirty seconds before the hellpod, given the respect they deserve.
changes: Drop Bay opens on the moment before you dive: your slot, three for your squad, and what the mission and planet will ask of you.
Choose a loadout, then confirm it. Until you do, the squad warnings leave you out, so a half picked kit never raises a false alarm.
The picker keeps the hard rules: no heat venting builds on a hot planet, nothing built for another difficulty.
The grid of every build moved to its own tab.

title: Ironclad Democracy arrives
say: Eleven new tools of liberation, and the ratings caught up with the game.
changes: Eleven new items, eight of them from the Ironclad Democracy warbond.
Ratings re-read from u.gg for patch 7.1.1, each list stamped with the patch it was voted on.
Five ratings moved. The Orbital Precision Strike is S+ everywhere now.
All nineteen patch caveats retired: every vote now postdates the change it was warning about.
The Meltamine is the Melta Mine, as the game spells it. Saved builds still find it.

title: Accounts, built and switched off
say: Classified groundwork. Citizens need not concern themselves.
changes: There is now a small server that can hold accounts. It is switched off, and the tool never asks who you are.
It stays off until a forgotten password can be recovered. An account you can be locked out of forever helps nobody.
Support no longer claims there is no server, because now there is one.

title: A new home on Cloudflare
say: Relocated to a more defensible position. No casualties.
changes: The tool is served from Cloudflare. Same screens, same everything.
Fonts come from the tool itself, so opening it no longer tells Google you visited.
The page refuses anything from any other address: no outside scripts, styles, fonts or images.
Art and fonts are cached for a year; the page checks for updates every visit.

title: A build is scored as a build
say: Nine items, one verdict. The Ministry approves of teamwork.
changes: Every loadout carries two readings: what its gear is worth where you are dropping, and what the nine pieces are worth together.
Armour penetration counts again, for the whole build, and only for what you aim. An orbital does not find weak points.
A build that leaves a hole is told which one: nothing for armour, nothing for the crowd, nothing to close a fabricator.
The builder recomputes as you edit, so you can watch a gap close.
Every loadout rule is tested against 300 random builds before it ships. Two were cut for describing the pool instead of the build.

title: Peril, and a column that stopped hiding
say: Being outnumbered and going deep are the same problem. Both now count.
changes: Difficulty and squad size combine into one number, peril, and the stealth advice scales along it instead of switching on at a cutoff.
How much a second player helps is taken from the game's own patrol figures, not guessed.
Our rating appears as soon as you pick a front. It used to wait for a planet that most sessions never set.
Rules no longer force a tier. Everything is points, so weapons keep the order they already stood in.
Two ideas the rules kept repeating, long range and suppressed, are now tags on the weapons, each saying where it came from.

title: Sandstorms are weather, not a climate
say: A three minute sandstorm is not a lifestyle.
changes: Two rules making opposite absolute claims no longer quietly overrule each other. The points decide.
Sandstorms and blizzards cost less and cap nothing. They come and go; heat and cold do not.
Alone, a storm is partly a gift: it blinds them as much as you. Solo on bots in a sandstorm, the Censor now tops the list.

title: The tier badge is a stamped plate
say: Freshly pressed at the Super Earth Mint.
changes: Every tier is a stamped plate with a stencil letter, in a new ladder: S+ red, S yellow, A purple, B blue, C green, D grey.
Pick the badge's finish in Settings. Changing theme never moves it.
Nothing ever fades or shrinks a badge to say a rating is low. A D reads as clearly as an S+.

title: How many of you are dropping
say: Solo on Impossible and four on Impossible are different wars.
changes: Squad size joins the scenario, and rules can read it along with difficulty.
Solo on bots at 7 and up, suppressed weapons take over: a sentry dies without waking the base behind it.
The crowd's vote has six S+ primaries on bots and not one is suppressed. That is the gap this tool exists to fill.

title: The scenario is a screen, not a panel on every tab
say: One choice, shown once. Six copies of it was excessive even for propaganda.
changes: Where you are dropping is its own screen, behind a one line bar above the list.
Difficulty shows the game's own marks in the game's own colours.
Both rating columns are sort buttons; the one you are sorting by is the solid one.

title: The row shows the numbers
say: Less apologising, more ballistics.
changes: Weapon rows show what the wiki publishes: magazine and spares, fire rate, ergonomics, recoil, sway, stagger and durable damage.
What is genuinely still missing, reload time and projectile count, is still admitted.

title: Armour stops downgrading half the list
say: Charging 48 rifles for being rifles was not justice.
changes: Enemy armour no longer moves single item ratings. It was marking down 42 of 51 Automaton primaries for having identical armour readings.
The facts stay on every row. They come back as a rating once whole loadouts are scored.
A rule health check now flags any rule that fires on most of what it looks at.

title: A roadmap in the menu
say: What is coming, minus the promises. Dates are for Major Orders.
changes: One timeline, one line per milestone, with the one thing actually next lit up.
Every unbuilt item says what it waits on, and none carries a date.

title: Say what difficulty you play at
say: No more warnings about Factory Striders on Trivial.
changes: Difficulty is part of the scenario, and ratings count only the enemies you can meet at that level.
Fixed an Illuminate roster that never exists: Vote Snatchers replace the regulars rather than join them.

title: It is a scenario, not a brief
say: A brief is handed to you. A scenario is what you are walking into.
changes: Front, planet, biome, hazards and mission are now called the scenario everywhere. Nothing you had set was lost.

title: Armour penetration has something to measure against
say: 80 enemies, 594 body parts, all of them catalogued for freedom.
changes: Every weapon says what its penetration opens on your front, and what it bounces off.
The rule is the game's own: above the armour value is full damage, equal is 65%, below is a ricochet.
Special strains and brigades are kept out of the reckoning for a normal drop.

title: A better planet source
say: Twelve planets rejoined the galaxy. Welcome back.
changes: Planets come from the community dataset, which knows all 281, with map positions and 339 supply lines.
Hazards stopped losing half their answer, and normal temperature stopped counting as one.

title: The second rating column goes live
say: The crowd's opinion, and ours, side by side. Dissent is logged, not punished.
changes: Say where you are dropping and every row gets a second rating, beside the community's, never replacing it.
Every point of movement carries a sentence. Tap a row to see which rules fired and what each was worth.
Seventy missions by their game names, each with the line its name does not tell you.

title: Difficulty gets names, planets get a picker
say: Nobody says difficulty 7. They say Suicide Mission.
changes: Difficulty is a slider over all ten levels with the game's own names and marks.
Search 281 planets and the biome and hazards fill themselves in, each hazard saying what it does to you.
Item names are readable on a phone.

title: Pick a front first
say: You chose your war before you opened the tool. Now the tool knows it too.
changes: The front is chosen above the list, not filtered inside it, and remembered.
Three faction columns became two rating columns: the community vote, and ours.
Tier list filters survive a trip to another page.

title: Vehicles and call-in codes
say: Exosuits, FRVs and a tank destroyer. Spare no expense.
changes: All eight vehicles and exosuits, rated.
Every stratagem carries its cooldown and its call-in code.

title: The stats this tool never had
say: And a hot planet bug that had been sabotaging plasma users all along.
changes: Magazine, fire rate, recoil and the rest, fetched from the wiki.
Hot planets only rule out builds that can actually overheat: ten items, not twenty six.
Heat and cold effects are the game's real multipliers.

title: A phone gets its screen back
say: Less chrome, more democracy per pixel.
changes: On a phone the header and tabs are one 44 pixel row.
The page header lines up with the sidebar. The Bile Titan skin has its Terminid mark.

title: About, Support and this changelog
say: Paperwork. Super Earth runs on it.
changes: The tool became the Democracy Deployment System, with its name kept in one place for the next rename.
About, Support, a footer naming Arrowhead and Sony as unaffiliated, and this changelog.

title: Warbond skins
say: Ten new uniforms. Regulation colours only.
changes: Ten skins on top of Dark, Light and Neon, each with its own atmosphere: tracers on the Creek, rain for the ODSTs, gas over Entrenched Division.

title: Squads, roles and profiles
say: The first squad readout. Morale is mandatory.
changes: Role tags for anti-armour, crowd control and objectives, and a squad panel that says what is going to hurt.
Named ownership profiles, so a second player's collection lives apart from yours.

title: Stable ids, the Builder and Drop Bay
say: Every item got a serial number. Renames no longer lose your gear.
changes: Items keyed by stable ids, so a rename never orphans what you saved.
The Loadout Builder, with the tier list as its picker, and Drop Bay as a grid of builds.

title: Out of the artifact, into a real project
say: Field promoted from prototype to tool.
changes: Ported to a proper project with identical behaviour, export and import, a sidebar, and four themes.

title: The 7.0.0 data rebuild
say: 17 wrong ratings, 38 wrong sources and 2 wrong names, corrected for the record.
changes: Rebuilt from the per item tables: complete coverage, 29 missing items added.

title: The original artifact
say: Where it all began: one file and a lot of opinions.
changes: A single file tier browser with lock sets, favourites, hard biome gates, and 39 curated loadouts.
